title: Precision pilot weekly hypothesis triage
summary: Weekly sync to triage hypothesis about INT8 vs FP8 quality deltas observed in the pilot. Reviewed recent batch runs, discussed sensitivity sweep results, KV cache interactions, and a fallback plan for user-facing regressions. Agreed on next experiments and owners.
topics: throughput and tail latency under batching
KV/prefix cache impact on perf and quality
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jenna (BlueHelix ML), Tom (Infra), Priya (Product)

Summary: weekly POC checkpoint for precision pilot; focus on hypothesis triage and next experiments.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, welcome, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, is that still good?
[00:08] Jenna (BlueHelix): yeah that works for us, thanks maya. we've got the usual suspects on our side, tom and priya.
[00:12] Tom (BlueHelix): hey, morning from my side. quick note - we're still on the staging V P C with the dedicated nodes.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood): awesome. agenda: recap last week's runs, go over the sensitivity sweep results for F P eight and in t eight, KV cache interactions, then decide next actions.
[00:32] Priya (BlueHelix): sounds good. we hit a few surprising drops in conversational benchmarks on FP8 yesterday, so keen to understand tradeoffs.
[01:05] Maya: ok quick recap - two baseline runs: float16 baseline and the INT8/FP8 variants. FP8 seemed to drop on the NLU category by ~3.2% on our internal metric, int8 was closer but had some tail latency wins.
[01:22] Jenna: yeah the NLU drop is the main blocker for us. the recommendation was to try the mixed-layer quant profile and increase KV cache warmup; we ran both but results were noisy.
[02:10] Carlos: right, noise is expected — small sample sizes + prefix variability. we did a sensitivity sweep across 2k prompts and added random seed seeds and saw clusters: FP8 regressed mainly on long-context prompts with entity resolution.
[02:45] Tom: can you clarify long context? like > 1024 tokens or more? we were assuming 2k was the max in these tests.
[02:52] Carlos: yep we had buckets: 512, 1k, 2k. FP8 delta gets worse in the 1k-2k bucket. seems related to KV cash compression artifacts over many steps, so the K V cache behavior matters.
[03:18] Jenna: K V cash? you mean KV cache — sometimes the transcript does that in our notes.
[03:21] Carlos: sorry, yes, KV cache. transcription autocorrect.
[04:00] Priya: is this something we could mitigate with selective layer FP16 fallback for attention layers?
[04:07] Carlos: exactly one hypothesis: keep first and last attention blocks at FP16, quantize middle layers — 'selective dequant' profile. We saw that reduces the NLU drop to ~1%.
[04:50] Maya: note that selective fallback increases memory and slight latency — about +6% p50 in our runs. you had concerns about latency budgets, tom?
[05:05] Tom: yes for user facing we target p95 < 450ms. with selective fallback we were hitting p95 around 520ms on bursty traffic in staging. batching policy interacts a lot here.
[05:35] Jenna: what about smarter batching: smaller max batch but more frequent flush? we tried continuous batching but saw cost spikes.
[06:00] Carlos: there's a tradeoff. continuous batching helps throughput but increases p95 tails. we can tune batch window and max tokens; suggestion: enable dynamic batching with time cap 20ms and max batch 8 for the pilot. our internal sim showed p95 down ~12% vs unconstrained batching.
[06:42] Priya: ok that's worth trying. what about cache TTL and warmup? last run had cold starts for a segment of users.
[06:54] Carlos: increase prefix caching TTL and do pre-warm on known session ids; also consider prefix dedup so similar sessions reuse cached KV. that reduced token compute in our sim by ~14%.
[07:20] Maya: quick question from product: how feasible is automatic fallback to float16 when quality drift crosses threshold? can we do auto rollback?
[07:35] Carlos: yes, Redwood supports rollout policies and automatic fallback. we can define an eval set and a regression threshold (e.g., >1.5% on the NLU eval) to trigger failover to a pinned float16 variant.
[07:55] Jenna: that would be great — we want automatic protection in case FP8 regresses in production.
[08:10] Maya: we'll propose a rollout policy: start canary at 5% traffic, run 4-hour eval windows, if metric delta >1.5% revert. Carlos, can you draft the policy?
[08:20] Carlos: yep i'll put a policy draft in the shared doc.
[09:00] Tom: security quick check — any change to data residency or logs with these experiments? we need to ensure logs remain in our region and KMS keys unchanged.
[09:12] Maya: no change to residency; the pilot is running in your region. we will not export raw payloads. Redwood logs tokens counts and perf metrics, audit logs are available if you want them to ship to your SIEM.
[09:30] Jenna: can we get the SOC2/ISO stub again? last week i misplaced the link.
[09:38] Maya: sure i'll re-send the security pack after the call.
[10:00] Priya: back to quality — you mentioned the sensitivity sweep, can you walk the numbers?
[10:12] Carlos: sure — topline: FP8 overall delta -2.9% on NLU, but distribution: 60% of prompts unaffected, 25% small drift (-0.5 to -1.5%), 15% significant (-3 to -7%). INT8 had -1.1% overall with better tail but slight degradation in factual recall.
[11:05] Jenna: the significant bucket — examples? were those heavy entity disambiguation ones?
[11:12] Carlos: yes many involved long instruction context + entity resolution and code formatting. one example where FP8 hallucinated a version number.
[11:40] Tom: about hallucinations — did you see any correlation with temperature or decoding strategy?
[11:50] Carlos: most runs used top-p 0.95 with beam width 1 (sampling). we re-ran greedy and saw similar deltas, so likely quant-induced weight perturbation, not decoding randomness.
[12:15] Maya: action item: compile 20 failing prompts and a minimal repro with seeds, Carlos to own.
[12:20] Carlos: noted.
[12:30] Jenna: also can we get the exact model binary/commit used for the FP8 build? we want to archive it for audits.
[12:40] Maya: yes we'll tag the build and share the artifact link.
[13:10] Priya: on performance numbers, can you call out throughput differences? we saw int8 had 1.8x throughput vs FP16, FP8 had 2.3x but with quality variance.
[13:25] Carlos: that's aligned: FP8 gives more perf but less numeric stability on long contexts. INT8 gave modest perf with fewer regressions.
[14:00] Tom: for production, leaning towards INT8 with selective FP16 fallback sounds reasonable if rollback windows are automated. cost-wise what's delta?
[14:12] Maya: rough estimate — INT8 gives ~40% lower token compute cost vs FP16; FP8 ~55% lower but you pay in risk. we'll put a more precise cost table in the next email.
[14:40] Jenna: can we schedule a direct benchmark where Redwood runs our 10k prompt suite across all variants (FP16, INT8, FP8, selective-fallback) with p95/p99 reported? we need reproducible numbers.
[14:54] Carlos: yes we can run that — need access to the prompt set and the seed mapping. please drop them in the shared drive.
[15:10] Priya: timeline for that run? we're hoping for results by early next week.
[15:18] Carlos: we can do a prioritized run overnight if you provide the suite today, deliverables by Monday EOD.
[15:30] Maya: next, quick discussion about routing policies — can we route high-value traffic to INT8-FP16 blended variants and bulk low-value to FP8?
[15:40] Carlos: yep routing by traffic tag and model variant is supported. we can use header-based routing or token thresholds.
[16:00] Tom: fine-grained routing means infra complexity — we'll need rollout docs and runbooks.
[16:12] Maya: we'll produce a runbook — Carlos to draft.
[16:20] Jenna: any blockers on your side to proceed with the sensitivity sweep repruns?
[16:28] Tom: infra wise we're good, just need the artifact and access tokens refreshed.
[16:38] Maya: i'll rotate a staging token and share.
[16:45] Carlos: ok owners recap and next steps coming up.
[16:50] Maya: any other questions?
[16:55] Priya: just one — is there a recommended guardrail for user-visible features when we run FP8? like confidence scoring?
[17:05] Carlos: yes add a conservatism heuristic: for low-confidence outputs based on logit gap, route to fallback. simple thresholding worked in our tests.
[17:25] Maya: good call. alright, we'll wrap.

End transcript.
